dimension_justifications.soundness: The primary capacity claim is sound and unusually well normalized. I independently rebuilt the Appendix C component model (bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4), n=2048T residual, 512T per attention K and V, 32,768 conv + 524,288 recurrent per GDN layer, T=3807.25) and it reproduces 136.235 / 34.683 / 9.661 / 9.395 / 7.536 / 56.438 MiB exactly, so the Store column is arithmetically self-consistent, and the authors' own correction of the FP32/BF16 confound (14.10x physical vs 10.9965x like-for-like, Sec. 5.2, App. C p. 17) is exactly the kind of normalization most papers omit. Interval discipline is also strong: resampling unit, resample count, interval type, seed and seed-sensitivity are all stated (App. B p. 15), all 42 intervals are inventoried with the reference arm each one actually used (Table 3), and the text repeatedly refuses to read a zero-crossing interval as equivalence. What holds the score at 3 rather than 4 is that the paper's second headline -- 5.84x smaller than a quantized exact cache at 3.41 F1 points better (Abstract, Sec. 5.2, Sec. 5.4, Conclusion) -- has two substantive defects: the comparison arm is not bit-width matched (I show the 5.84x factors exactly as 3.918x split-depth times 1.491x bit-width, issue ISS-01), and the asserted 3.41-point quality advantage has no paired interval at all despite both arms living in one execution over the same 60 items (ISS-02). Two further gaps touch the paper's most important metric: the Store definition asserted twice in the PDF is contradicted by the submitted provenance (ISS-05), and the claimed exact cross-table reconciliation does not close arithmetically (ISS-06). None of these invalidates the central capacity result, but each one bites a claim the paper actually makes.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Captions, scope notes and the cohort-to-claim table (Table 7) are exemplary: every table states its cohort, statistic, denominator and explicit exclusions, blank cells are declared unmeasured rather than zero, and Sec. 5.6 plus Appendix I enumerate non-claims at a level of candour well above the norm. The problems are localized but real. The abstract quotes 8-item timing medians (0.163 s, ~0.673 s, 13.38 vs 7.15-7.19 tok/s, 54.11 ms) immediately after establishing a 60-item cohort and never flags the switch, even though a 60-item TTFT measurement exists and is not the one quoted (ISS-04). Sec. 5.2 p. 7 says 'Uniform Q4 and the aggressive mixed policy go further still (Table 2)' when the aggressive row is a 60-item mean in Table 1 and uniform Q4 an 8-item median in Table 2, mixing cohorts and mis-citing the table (ISS-08). Sec. 5.4 calls the operating-point run 'an independent run' that 'reproduces' the archival result while Sec. 5.6 says 'none replicates another' (ISS-07). Table 1's Recall column is empty in all ten rows and the dense arm's Store reads '-' in one block and 0.000 in the other. Figure 2's per-layer bit strip is correct ([8,8,8,4,8,8,8]) but illegible at print size.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The genuinely new object is the accounting unit, not a mechanism: the paper concedes that group-wise asymmetric quantization, per-layer width assignment and split-depth reuse are all prior art (Sec. 2), and its contribution is to apply them to the whole hybrid split-replay entry -- residual plus lower KV plus conv/recurrent state -- under one declared denominator, plus the ForkAudit ownership rail. That is a fair and useful correction to how CoMem-style methods are counted. But the demonstrated value is narrow on the paper's own numbers: one model, one hardware family, 60 items, one split depth validated against exactly one alternative; TTFT is roughly 4x worse than exact reuse and, on the 60-item run, worse than dense recomputation too (0.656 s vs 0.636 s), so the operating point pays off only in the capacity-bound multi-document regime the paper explicitly does not evaluate (no continuous batching, admission, eviction, QPS or NVML capacity, Sec. 5.6). The allocator result is the saving from block sharing against a full-copy control the authors themselves call not an optimized baseline, and their audited fork ties paged attention on both endpoints while costing 1.93 GiB more generation increment (Table 18). ForkAudit is thorough but runs on full-prefix BF16 KV with no split depth and no quantization, i.e. not on the proposed method, so the ownership guarantee for the packed Read path transfers by design argument only.

paper_summary: The paper proposes Q-CoMem, a capacity-first extension of CoMem split replay for a hybrid attention/GDN LLM (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on H20-3e). An offline Write executes a document to split depth j=7 and group-quantizes the whole retained entry -- the boundary residual, the lower full-attention KV, and the lower convolution/recurrent state -- with per-state-type widths; an online Read dequantizes, forks the entry with request-local mutable state, replays the query through the lower layers and reconstructs the suffix. A separate fail-closed trace protocol, ForkAudit, validates a seven-target ownership contract (immutability, COW, recurrent rebinding, call provenance) over a 96-configuration factorial. The headline empirical results are: on a 60-item Qasper/2WikiMQA cohort a frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy cuts mean retained tensor payload from 136.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (14.10x; 10.9965x against an all-BF16 reference) at a paired mean F1 difference of -0.45 points [-2.06, 0.99] against full-prefix; a separately executed run on the same items adds a full-prefix Q8 exact-cache arm at 56.438 MiB and -3.78 [-9.12, 0.32], giving a claimed 5.84x capacity advantage at 3.41 higher mean F1; timing is adverse (TTFT ~0.163 s full-prefix vs ~0.673 s Q-CoMem on an 8-item slice, throughput 13.38 vs 7.15-7.19 tok/s, TPOT within 2.5%); and shared-document KV cuts a post-priming allocator delta 54.5% final / 42.2% peak at N=32 against a full-copy control, tying a paged-prefix baseline. The paper explicitly disclaims recall, total process memory, edge performance, TTFT acceleration and broad quality preservation.
strongest_verified_contribution: The whole-entry retained-state accounting for a hybrid split-replay entry, together with the dtype normalization that separates packing from dtype narrowing. I verified this independently: rebuilding the Appendix C component model from first principles (residual 2048T values, layer-3 K and V 512T each, six GDN layers of 32,768 conv + 524,288 recurrent elements, packed size ceil(n/64)(8b+4)) reproduces every printed Store value in Tables 1 and 2 to the last decimal, including 136.235, 34.683, 9.661, 9.395, 7.536 and 56.438 MiB. The paper's disclosure that 30.000 of the 136.235 MiB reference is FP32 GDN recurrent state in excess of BF16, and its consequent reporting of both 14.10x and 10.9965x, is a correction that materially changes the headline in the honest direction and is fully checkable from the PDF alone (Sec. 5.2 p. 7, Table 1 footnote, App. C pp. 17).
strengths: Reference-arm discipline is close to airtight in the main tables: every ratio and every interval in Table 1 names the arm it uses, the two executions occupy separate blocks that are never pooled, and each block is differenced against its own full-prefix row. I checked all ten deltas against the printed means and all six displayed intervals against Table 3; every one matches (e.g. 54.24-54.68=-0.45 from unrounded -0.4455; 54.297-54.668=-0.37).

Appendix B (p. 15) publishes a complete interval inventory -- all 42 paired bootstrap intervals, including the 24 archival ones with the reference arm each actually used -- explicitly so that no interval is 'computed but unreported'. It also discloses that the previously published -0.39 was against split Q16 and understated the deployment-relevant loss by ~13%, which is a self-correction against the authors' own interest.

Bootstrap specification is complete for the new intervals: unit (paired item-level over the 60 common (dataset, source index) keys), count (10,000), method (percentile), seed (20260902/20260903), and a Monte-Carlo sensitivity check across five seeds bounding endpoint movement at 0.075 points. The text never converts a zero-crossing interval into equivalence and states so explicitly in the Table 1 footnote and Sec. 5.4.

The negative and self-undercutting results are reported with the same prominence as the positive ones: TTFT is worse than exact reuse and, on the 60-item run, worse than dense recomputation; ForkAudit did not run on the quantized Read path; the 54.5%/42.2% allocator saving is block sharing that the audited fork merely ties, at 1.93 GiB worse generation increment (Table 18, Sec. 5.5); and the historical alias is caught by a plain persistent-base content invariant too, so the audit's increment is localization, not exclusive detection.

Appendix C converts an apparent format violation (34.683/9.661 = 3.590x above the 3.5556x Q4 ceiling) into an explanation rather than hiding it, showing the normalized step is 2.969x and that the printed 3.590x mixes packing with dtype narrowing. The Eq. 3 format identity is reported as satisfied on 180/180 quantized item-policy pairs.

Table 7's cohort-to-claim authorization matrix and Appendix I's expanded limitations state, per cohort, the exact inference authorized and the inference explicitly excluded -- an unusually strong defence against silent scope creep.
questions: What does a width-matched quantized exact cache retain and score? Applying your own frozen bit vector (Q4 attention, Q8 GDN) to the unsplit entry gives 37.85 MiB/document from your Table 4 components, i.e. 3.92x the frozen point rather than 5.84x. Please report that arm's Store and F1, or state why Q8 rather than the method's own widths is the right exact-cache comparator.

Please report the paired item-level bootstrap interval for frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 (j=7) minus full-prefix Q8 on the operating-point run. Both arms are in one execution over the same 60 items, so the interval is a few lines of the analysis you already ran. Does it exclude zero?

What is the run identifier, artifact package and manifest hash for the operating-point run (seed 20260903)? It appears in neither Table 30 nor the submitted claim_evidence_map.tsv nor method_provenance.tsv, yet it supplies the exact-cache arm, the j=13 control and all 60-item TTFT numbers.

What generation budget did the archival 60-item panel use? The PDF states it for the 8-item panel (at most 32 tokens) and describes the operating-point run as 'dataset-length generation', but never states it for the archival panel that produces the headline F1 values.

Please give the run-to-run spread (min/max or IQR over the three repeats) for every TTFT, TPOT and tokens/s cell in Tables 1, 2, 21 and 22. Without it the 'TPOT within 2.5%' conclusion cannot be evaluated.

Section 5.1 says the two implementations 'agree to the byte' with '0.000 MiB left to the accounting' and attributes the 136.235-vs-140.34 gap to a cohort '3.8%' longer. Your own component model implies the 8-item median document is ~4,017 tokens, i.e. 5.5% longer than the 3807.25-token cohort mean. Which document-length statistics were compared, and can both be printed?

Sec. 5.4 calls the operating-point run 'an independent run' that 'reproduces' the archival result, while Sec. 5.6 says 'none replicates another'. Which is intended, and on what basis is a re-execution over the identical 60 items on the identical stack independent?

Figure 1 and Figure 2c show Read dequantizing 'to BF16', but M-QCOMEM-EQ3-DEQUANTIZER states PackedTensor.dequantize restores original_dtype, so an FP32 GDN leaf round-trips to FP32. Which is the executed behaviour, and does it affect the Read-side working set?

issues.location: Abstract lines 032-036 (p. 1); Sec. 1 contribution bullet 2 (p. 2); Sec. 5.2 p. 7 ('an exact cache packed with the same codec'); Sec. 5.4 p. 8; Conclusion p. 9; Table 1 operating-point block row 'Full-prefix Q8'
issues.observed_evidence: The quantized exact-cache comparison is not bit-width matched, and the paper never says so. Full-prefix Q8 stores every attention layer at 8 bits, whereas the frozen policy stores the residual and layer-3 attention at 4 bits and only the GDN state at 8 bits. Rebuilding both arms from the paper's own Table 4 components (attention K or V at Q4 = 1.0457 MiB/layer; GDN layer at Q8 = 0.5644 MiB) gives: full-prefix Q8 = 20x1.9752 + 30x0.5644 = 56.44 MiB (matches the printed 56.438); the same bit vector as the frozen policy applied to the unsplit entry = 20x1.0457 + 30x0.5644 = 37.85 MiB. Therefore the headline 5.84x decomposes exactly as 3.918x (split depth, 37.85/9.661) times 1.491x (bit width, 56.438/37.85). Only the 3.918x is attributable to split replay, and it coincides with the paper's own split-Q16 factor of 3.93x. No width-matched exact-cache arm appears anywhere in the paper (grep confirms 'full-prefix Q8' is the only full-prefix quantized arm). The paper performs precisely this kind of normalization for the FP32/BF16 confound in Appendix C but not for the bit-width confound in the arm it introduced this revision.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the paper's second headline number and the only comparison against a competitive quantized baseline; it appears in the abstract, an intro contribution bullet, Sec. 5.2, Sec. 5.4 and the conclusion. A reader takes 5.84x as the capacity advantage of split replay over quantized exact caching, when 25% of the log-ratio comes from the baseline being stored at twice the bit width of the method. The paper's own standard, set in Appendix C ('Both numerator and denominator must be stated under one dtype convention'), is violated by its own newest comparison. Describing the arm as 'an exact cache packed with the same codec' compounds this: the codec is the same, the bit vector is not, and the sentence invites the opposite reading.
issues.required_fix: Add a width-matched full-prefix arm using the frozen bit vector (Q4 residual-equivalent/attention, Q8 GDN) to the operating-point run and report its Store and mean F1 with a paired interval against the run's full-prefix reference. In the abstract, intro, Sec. 5.2 and the conclusion, either quote the width-matched ratio or decompose 5.84x explicitly into its split-depth and bit-width factors. Replace 'the same codec' with 'the same codec at a uniform 8-bit width', and drop or qualify 'the strongest quantized exact cache we measured' unless a width sweep supports 'strongest'.
issues.verification_test: From Table 4, recompute 20x(attention K/V at the frozen width) + 30x(GDN layer at Q8) and confirm 37.85 MiB/document; check that 37.85/9.661 = 3.918 and 56.438/37.85 = 1.491, and that 3.918 x 1.491 = 5.84. Then confirm the revised text quotes the split-attributable factor wherever 5.84x currently appears unqualified.
issues.evidence_needed: One additional configuration on the existing 60-item operating-point execution (full prefix, frozen bit vector), reporting Store, mean F1, and the paired bootstrap interval against that run's full-prefix arm.

issues.location: Abstract lines 033-036 (p. 1); Sec. 1 contribution bullet 2 (p. 2); Sec. 5.4 p. 8; Conclusion p. 9 lines 480-482; Table 1 footnote p. 7
issues.observed_evidence: The paper asserts a 3.41-point mean-F1 advantage of frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 over full-prefix Q8 (54.297 vs 50.885) in the abstract, the intro bullet, Sec. 5.4 and the conclusion, but states in Sec. 5.4 and the Table 1 footnote that 'none was computed between two non-reference arms' and that 'their intervals against the shared reference overlap'. Those two intervals are -3.78 [-9.12, 0.32] and -0.37 [-1.97, 1.08]; both cross zero and overlap over roughly [-1.97, 0.32], so the ordering the paper asserts is not established at any stated confidence level. Both arms come from one execution over the same 60 items with the same item keys, so the paired item-level bootstrap the paper already implements (M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP: pairing on (dataset, id, source_index), 10,000 resamples) applies directly with no new measurement.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the paper's own stated standard applied unevenly. It computed 18 additional intervals in this revision specifically so that its comparisons would use the arm they name, and Appendix B opens by promising that no interval exists unreported. Yet the single most decision-relevant pair -- the proposed operating point against the strongest competing baseline -- is the one pair with no interval, and the number is nevertheless promoted to the abstract and the conclusion without the caveat that appears in Sec. 5.4. A reader of the abstract alone would take the quality advantage as measured rather than as a point estimate whose sign is not resolved.
issues.required_fix: Compute and report the paired item-level bootstrap interval for (frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, j=7) minus (full-prefix Q8) on the operating-point run, with the same unit, count, method and seed as the others, and add it to the Table 3 inventory. If it crosses zero, remove the bare '3.41-point higher mean F1' from the abstract, the intro bullet and the conclusion, or attach the interval there. Keep the retained-state ordering, which is deterministic and does not need an interval.
issues.verification_test: Recompute the paired difference over the 60 common keys from the operating-point per-item F1 values with 10,000 resamples at the registered seed; confirm the point estimate is 3.41 and report the percentile endpoints. Then confirm every occurrence of '3.41' in the PDF carries either that interval or an explicit statement that the difference is not resolved.
issues.evidence_needed: The operating-point run's 60 per-item F1 values for the frozen j=7 and full-prefix Q8 arms; no re-execution required.

issues.location: Table 1 operating-point block (p. 7); Sec. 5.1 p. 6; Reproducibility Statement p. 10; Appendix J Table 30 (pp. 34-36)
issues.observed_evidence: The operating-point run is the source of the full-prefix Q8 exact-cache arm (56.438 MiB, -3.78), the j=13 control (16.101 MiB, -3.40), all five 60-item TTFT values, and the seed-20260903 intervals. It has no row in the paper's own artifact and claim map (Table 30, which lists 'Q-CoMem 60-item Store-F1 validation' for the archival package and 'Mac and H20 deployment controls' for the 8-item timing package, but nothing for this run), and it has no entry in either submitted artifact file: grepping claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv for 56.438, 16.101, 20260903, 50.885, 54.297, 0.656, 0.181, 'operating-point' and 'j=13' returns zero hits in both files. The Reproducibility Statement says the block is 'recorded under its own run identifier' but never gives that identifier, package path, or manifest hash. By contrast, every other cohort in the paper has both a Table 30 row and a registry entry.
issues.why_it_matters: Under pdf_plus_repository access this is the one experimental block a reviewer cannot check at all: it supplies the baseline comparison that this revision was evidently built around, and it is the only 60-item TTFT evidence in the paper. The paper's central methodological selling point is auditable claim-to-evidence binding; an unregistered block sitting in the headline table undercuts that specific selling point more than it would in an ordinary submission. It also makes ISS-02 unresolvable from the artifacts alone, since the per-item F1 values needed for the missing interval are not reachable.
issues.required_fix: Add a Table 30 row and a claim_evidence_map entry for the operating-point run naming its package alias, manifest SHA-256, run identifier and replay entry point, on the same terms as the archival package; add a method_provenance entry for its runner, timing instrumentation and bootstrap call site. State in Sec. 5.1 whether the block's Store column was measured in that execution or carried over from the archival accounting, since 136.235 and 9.661 are byte-identical across the two blocks.
issues.verification_test: Grep the revised claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv for 56.438, 16.101 and 20260903 and require non-zero hits bound to a manifest hash; confirm Table 30 lists the package; run the named replay and require it to regenerate the five operating-point rows and the two displayed intervals.
issues.evidence_needed: The operating-point run's archive alias, manifest hash, per-item shards and replay script, registered on the same terms as E-QCOMEM-60-VALIDATION-20260812D-A.

issues.location: Abstract lines 036-040 (p. 1); compare Sec. 5.1 'Latency execution' p. 6 and Table 2 p. 8
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract opens 'On an archival 60-item Qasper/2WikiMQA validation cohort...' and then, with no cohort switch marked, reports 'full-prefix Q16 reaches the first token in 0.163 s against about 0.673 s and has higher generated-token throughput (13.38 versus 7.15-7.19 tokens/s), while TPOT is within 2.5% of its 54.11 ms value'. Every one of those numbers is an 8-item median from Table 2 (source indices 6-9 of each dataset), not a 60-item statistic. A 60-item TTFT measurement does exist in the same paper (0.181 s full-prefix, 0.656 s frozen, Table 1 operating-point block) and is not the one quoted; throughput and TPOT were never measured on 60 items at all. The intro (p. 2) does disclose 'a separate execution on an eight-item subset', and Sec. 5.1 and Table 2 are scrupulous, so the failure is confined to the abstract -- the part of the paper most readers will use.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central procedural commitment is that cohorts are never pooled and every number carries its cohort and statistic (Sec. 5.1, Table 1 footnote, Table 7). The abstract silently violates that commitment for the entire latency paragraph, presenting an 8-item median as though it belonged to the 60-item panel introduced two sentences earlier. It also means the headline TTFT ratio (0.163 vs 0.673, ~4.1x) is not the one the larger cohort supports (0.181 vs 0.656, ~3.6x). The distinction between what rests on 60 items and what rests on 8 is exactly the distinction this paper asks to be judged on.
issues.required_fix: In the abstract, mark the cohort for every timing figure ('on an eight-item subset of that cohort'), or quote the 60-item TTFT values and state that TPOT and throughput were measured only on the eight-item subset. Apply the same marking to the conclusion's timing sentence.
issues.verification_test: Read the abstract in isolation and check that each of 0.163, 0.673, 13.38, 7.15-7.19 and 54.11 carries an explicit cohort size, and that no timing number is attributable by default to the 60-item cohort named in the preceding sentence.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Memory denominators' p. 6 ('Store is the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry'); Table 2 caption p. 8 ('Store is the byte-range union owned by one retained entry')
issues.observed_evidence: The PDF defines the Store denominator twice as the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry. The submitted provenance record M-QCOMEM-DEPLOY-STORE states that the eight-item deployment table's printed Store column is persistent_document_nbytes (the residual.nbytes + PackedCache.nbytes formula, taken as a median), that the byte-range union quantity computed alongside it is persistent_total_resident_nbytes, and explicitly that 'Table 2's caption claim that Store is the physical byte-range union is therefore not what the printed column measures'. M-QCOMEM-STORE-ACCOUNTANT separately describes the 60-item column as the same nbytes sum with a (device, data_ptr, storage_nbytes) dedup, noting the two paths agree numerically for every quantized arm 'in this cohort' because each packed leaf owns a freshly allocated, exactly sized storage -- an agreement that holds by construction for packed entries and is not asserted for the unpacked full-prefix reference.
issues.why_it_matters: Store is the paper's primary metric and every headline ratio is a ratio of Store values; the denominator's definition is therefore load-bearing. A reader who takes the PDF at its word believes the metric is a physical range union that would capture allocator padding and over-allocation in the unpacked reference arm, whereas the printed column is an element-count-derived nbytes sum. The two coincide for packed arms but need not for the native-dtype full-prefix cache that sits in every denominator. This does not change any printed number -- I reproduced them all from the component model -- but it means the stated estimand is not the measured estimand, which is the one thing a denominator section must get right.
issues.required_fix: State the measured estimand precisely in Sec. 5.1 and both table captions: the deduplicated sum of owned tensor storage bytes for the retained entry, with the dedup key named. If the byte-range union differs for the full-prefix reference, report both and say which is printed; if it provably coincides for all reported arms, state that and give the check. Reconcile the caption with the provenance record either way.
issues.verification_test: For each of the five retained configurations, print both persistent_document_nbytes and persistent_total_resident_nbytes and confirm equality (or report the gap) -- in particular for the full-prefix native-dtype arm, where the packed-leaf argument for their coincidence does not apply.
issues.evidence_needed: Both accountant values, per configuration, from the existing deployment shards.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Memory denominators' p. 6 ('a 60-item mean against a median over documents 3.8% longer -- with 0.000 MiB left to the accounting'); Table 2 caption p. 8 ('a cohort with 3.8% shorter documents')
issues.observed_evidence: The paper claims the 136.235-vs-140.34 and 9.661-vs-10.01 gaps are fully explained by cohort and statistic, with '0.000 MiB left to the accounting', and quantifies the cohort difference as 3.8%. Under the paper's own Appendix C model, full-prefix Store is affine in document length: 20480T bytes (ten attention layers, K and V) plus a length-independent 61.875 MiB (30 conv at 0.0625 + 30 recurrent at 2.0). Inverting 140.34 MiB gives T = 4017.4 tokens; inverting the frozen row's 10.01 MiB with its coefficient of 1728 bytes/token gives T = 4019.1. Against the stated cohort mean of 3807.25 tokens that is 5.5% longer, not 3.8%. The provenance record M-QCOMEM-DEPLOY-STORE independently states the deployment median is 'a 4,016-token median document', confirming ~5.5%. A 3.8% increase would predict 139.06 MiB, leaving 1.28 MiB unexplained rather than 0.000. Separately, the two blocks state the difference inconsistently as '3.8% longer' and '3.8% shorter', which cannot both hold.
issues.why_it_matters: The claim is not that the reconciliation is approximate but that it is exact, and it is the sentence that licenses the reader to treat two differently sized headline numbers for the same quantity as consistent. A stated percentage that is off by 45% of its own value, attached to a zero-residual claim, is the kind of detail that makes a careful reader distrust the rest of the accounting -- unfairly, since every printed Store value is in fact exactly reproducible. The PDF also gives no document-length statistic for the 8-item slice, so the reconciliation cannot be checked from the PDF alone at all; I could only close it using the provenance file.
issues.required_fix: Print the two length statistics being compared (60-item mean T = 3807.25 tokens; 8-item median T ~= 4,016 tokens) and the corrected percentage, and show the one-line affine reconciliation: 61.875 + 20480T/2^20 evaluated at each length. If the '3.8%' was computed on a different quantity (e.g. raw prompt tokens rather than the T entering Store), say which quantity and stop using it to justify a zero-residual claim.
issues.verification_test: Evaluate 61.875 + 20480*T/2^20 at T = 3807.25 and at the 8-item median T; require the first to equal 136.235 and the second to equal 140.34 to three decimals. Repeat with the frozen row's coefficient (1728 bytes/token, constant 3.386 MiB) against 9.661 and 10.01.
issues.evidence_needed: The 8-item slice's document-length distribution (median at minimum), already present in the deployment shards.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 p. 6 ('one warm-up, three repeats'); Sec. 5.3 p. 7-8; Table 1 TTFT column; Table 2 TTFT/TPOT/tok-s columns p. 8; Tables 21-22 pp. 29-30
issues.observed_evidence: Warm-ups (one) and repeats (three) are declared, and the aggregation rule is given as 'medians over the eight documents', but not a single dispersion statistic accompanies any timing number anywhere in the paper: no range, IQR, standard deviation or interval for TTFT, TPOT or tokens/s in Table 1, Table 2, Table 21 or Table 22. A grep for IQR, standard deviation, variance and dispersion returns matches only for the F1 analysis and the CPU replay wall-time appendix (which does report ranges, e.g. 100.146 s (99.248-110.526 s)) -- so the authors clearly know how to report spread and did so for a peripheral measurement but not for the headline latency panel. On this evidence Sec. 5.3 and the abstract conclude 'TPOT is within 2.5% of full-prefix (54.97-55.44 versus 54.11 ms)', and Sec. 5.3 asserts on the 60-item run that Q-CoMem at 0.656 s is 'slower to the first token than honest dense recomputation' at 0.636 s -- a 3% gap. Also, how the three repeats and eight documents are combined (median of per-document medians, or median over all 24 measurements) is never stated.
issues.why_it_matters: A 2.5% TPOT claim and a 3% TTFT ordering are both inside the range where repeat-to-repeat noise on a shared GPU plausibly lives, and neither can be assessed without spread. The latency panel is the paper's account of the cost side of its trade-off -- the thing that makes the capacity claim honest -- so its resolution matters as much as the memory side. The undeclared aggregation rule also makes the eight-item medians non-reproducible from the shards even for someone holding them.
issues.required_fix: Report min-max or IQR over the three repeats for every timing cell, state the aggregation rule explicitly (over repeats first, then over documents, or the reverse), and either qualify or drop conclusions whose margin is smaller than the observed spread -- in particular 'TPOT within 2.5%' and the 0.656-vs-0.636 s ordering against dense recomputation.
issues.verification_test: For each configuration, recompute the per-document per-repeat TTFT/TPOT/tok-s distribution from the 168 archived timing rows, report the spread, and confirm that the 2.5% TPOT band and the frozen-vs-dense TTFT ordering survive it.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-repeat timing rows already archived in the deployment package (168 rows) and the operating-point run's timing records.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Quality cohort' p. 6; Table 2 caption p. 8; Table 7 rows 'H20 archival Store-F1 validation' and 'H20 operating-point run' (pp. 21)
issues.observed_evidence: The generation budget of the archival 60-item panel -- the run producing every headline F1 value and every displayed interval -- is never stated in the PDF. Sec. 5.1 gives only 'official LongBench-v1 prompts and a 4,096-token input cap'; the operating-point run is described as 'dataset-length generation'; Table 2's eight-item panel states 'at most 32 generated tokens'. The provenance record M-QCOMEM-READ-GREEDY supplies what the PDF omits: max_new_tokens is 128 for Qasper and 32 for 2WikiMQA. So the 8-item timing slice, which the PDF calls 'a subset of the quality cohort', truncates Qasper generations to a quarter of the budget used in the quality panel. The PDF never mentions this, and never explains why the same items score ~39 F1 in Table 2 and ~54 in Table 1, attributing the Store gap to cohort and statistic but leaving the far larger F1 gap unaddressed.
issues.why_it_matters: Answer F1 depends directly on generation budget, so an unstated budget makes the paper's headline quality numbers uninterpretable and unreproducible from the PDF, and makes the 'subset' framing of Table 2 misleading: the eight items are a subset of the cohort but not of the measurement protocol. It also bears on ISS-09: the closeness of 54.24 and 54.30 across the two 60-item executions can only be assessed once both budgets are known.
issues.required_fix: State the decoding configuration for every cohort in Sec. 5.1 and in each table caption: greedy, and max_new_tokens per dataset (128 Qasper / 32 2WikiMQA for the archival and operating-point panels; 32 for both datasets in the timing panel). Add one sentence noting that the eight-item panel's Qasper budget differs from the quality panel's, so the two F1 levels are not comparable.
issues.verification_test: Check that Sec. 5.1 and the captions of Tables 1, 2 and 21 each name a per-dataset generation budget, and that no table pair with differing budgets is described as a subset measurement without that caveat.
issues.evidence_needed: None; the configuration is already recorded in the runner.

issues.location: Sec. 5.4 p. 8 lines 404-405 vs Sec. 5.6 p. 9 lines 452-454
issues.observed_evidence: Sec. 5.4 states that the operating point's -0.37 [-1.97, 1.08] 'also reproduces the archival cohort's -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] against the same reference arm in an independent run'. Sec. 5.6 states of the three executions that 'none replicates another'. The two executions use the same 60 items, the same model, the same hardware family and the same stack, so they are a re-execution, not an independent replication -- the paper applies exactly this distinction correctly to the eight-item panel ('a subset of the quality cohort, not an independent replication', Sec. 5.1). The two runs also do not agree exactly: full-prefix reads 54.68 in one block and 54.67 in the other, and the frozen point 54.24 vs 54.30, under greedy decoding on identical items, which the PDF nowhere explains.
issues.why_it_matters: 'Reproduces ... in an independent run' invites a reader to treat the two blocks as mutually corroborating evidence, which would be the one form of pooling the paper otherwise forbids. It is also a self-contradiction within two pages, which weakens the credibility of the surrounding scope statements that are otherwise the paper's strongest feature.
issues.required_fix: Replace 'independent run' with 'a separate re-execution of the same items on the same stack', and either delete 'reproduces' or state precisely what agreement is being claimed. Add one sentence explaining the source of the small run-to-run F1 differences under greedy decoding.
issues.verification_test: Confirm Sec. 5.4 and Sec. 5.6 make the same statement about the relationship between the two executions, and that the PDF names a mechanism for the 54.68-vs-54.67 and 54.24-vs-54.30 differences.
issues.evidence_needed: None; editorial, plus one sentence on determinism.

issues.location: Sec. 5.2 p. 7 lines 353-355 ('Uniform Q4 and the aggressive mixed policy go further still (Table 2)')
issues.observed_evidence: The sentence cites Table 2 for both policies, but the aggressive mixed policy appears only in Table 1's archival block (7.536 MiB, a 60-item mean) and not in Table 2 at all; uniform Q4 appears only in Table 2 (8.41 MiB, an 8-item median). 'Go further still' compares both against the frozen point's 9.661, a 60-item mean -- so the uniform-Q4 half of the comparison sets an 8-item median against a 60-item mean in a single clause. Elsewhere the paper states that the two panels are never pooled and that the 8-item documents are longer, which is precisely why 10.01 and 9.661 differ for the same policy.
issues.why_it_matters: It is a one-line lapse in the discipline the paper is built on, in the section that establishes the memory result, and it produces a comparison (8.41 < 9.661) that the paper's own cohort rules forbid -- the same policy on the 60-item cohort would not be 8.41.
issues.required_fix: Split the sentence: cite Table 1 for the aggressive mixed policy with its 60-item mean, and cite Table 2 for uniform Q4 with its eight-item median and an explicit note that it is not comparable to the 60-item column.
issues.verification_test: Check each policy named in Sec. 5.2 against the table that actually contains it and confirm every Store comparison in that paragraph is within one cohort and one statistic.

issues.location: Table 1 p. 7: Recall column (all ten rows blank); dense row Store '-' in the archival block vs 0.000 in the operating-point block; Table 3 first block p. 16 (split Q16 intervals)
issues.observed_evidence: Three small honesty-of-presentation defects in the headline table and its interval inventory. (a) The Recall column is present and empty in all ten rows of Table 1 and in Table 2; the paper states Recall was never measured in any cohort, so the column carries no information. (b) The same arm, no-cache dense recompute, has Store '-' in the archival block and 0.000 in the operating-point block, while the caption asserts 'blank cells are unmeasured metrics, not zeros' -- so the archival block reads as if dense's retained state were unknown, when Sec. 3 defines it as S(D)=0 by construction. (c) Several intervals in Table 3 are degenerate: split Q16 on 2WikiMQA is +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] and the pooled split Q16 interval is [-0.1754, +0.0000], reported without noting that they arise from per-item deltas that are almost all exactly zero rather than from a tight estimate.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's blank-cell convention is a deliberate and welcome device, but here it is applied inconsistently to the same quantity in adjacent blocks, and a percentile interval of exactly [0,0] presented alongside genuine intervals invites a reader to treat a degenerate resample distribution as a precision result.
issues.required_fix: Drop the Recall column and state once in the caption that Recall was not measured in any cohort; print 0.000 for the dense arm's Store in both blocks with a footnote that it is zero by construction, not a measurement; and mark the degenerate intervals in Table 3 (e.g. a footnote giving the number of non-zero per-item deltas behind each).
issues.verification_test: Confirm no all-blank column remains in Tables 1-2, that the dense Store entry is identical in both blocks, and that each interval whose width is 0 carries the count of non-zero per-item deltas.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-item delta counts, already in the archived shards.

issues.location: Figure 1 p. 3 ('Fetch + dequantize to BF16'); Figure 2c p. 5 ('Read: dequantize to BF16 request state'); Eq. 3 p. 4; App. B p. 15 ('The archived analysis records no bootstrap seed')
issues.observed_evidence: Three small PDF-versus-provenance mismatches. (a) Both figures state that Read dequantizes to BF16, but M-QCOMEM-EQ3-DEQUANTIZER records that PackedTensor.dequantize restores original_dtype, so an FP32 GDN recurrent leaf round-trips to FP32 -- relevant because the same FP32/BF16 asymmetry is what Appendix C spends a page normalizing on the Write side. (b) Eq. 3 omits the degenerate-group guard recorded in M-QCOMEM-EQ3-QUANTIZER (groups with u==m are assigned s=1 rather than s=0), and the flattened-order grouping with edge-value padding for cache leaves is likewise unstated. (c) App. B states 'The archived analysis records no bootstrap seed', while M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP records a base seed of 20260811 with deterministic per-comparison offsets and notes the resampler draws indices one at a time.
issues.why_it_matters: None of these changes a number, but each is a place where a reader reconstructing the method from the PDF would build something different from what ran. (a) affects the Read-side working set and sits directly on the paper's own dtype-normalization theme; (b) means Eq. 3 as printed is not the executed quantizer; (c) is a reproducibility statement contradicted by the submitted provenance.
issues.required_fix: Correct the figure labels to 'dequantize to the stored source dtype' or state the exception for FP32 recurrent state; add the u==m guard and the grouping/padding rule to Eq. 3 or a footnote; and reconcile App. B's seed statement with the provenance record, stating whether 20260811 was the seed in effect for the archived intervals.
issues.verification_test: Diff the printed quantizer/dequantizer description against the referenced source lines; confirm the figure labels match the executed dtype behaviour; confirm App. B and the provenance agree on the archived seed.
issues.evidence_needed: None beyond the already-submitted provenance file.

issues.location: Submitted artifact method_provenance.tsv (11 occurrences), e.g. records M-QCOMEM-STORE-ACCOUNTANT, M-QCOMEM-GROUP-64, M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP, M-QCOMEM-PANEL-RUNNER, M-QCOMEM-READ-GREEDY
issues.observed_evidence: The submitted method_provenance.tsv contains eleven absolute filesystem paths of the form /Users/<username>/... naming a 'live implementation tree' outside the artifact packages. Appendix A already discloses honestly that the run driver, aggregation and bootstrap scripts, layer-policy search, deployment accountant and launch script are not archived, and the provenance file marks the same files 'NOT ARCHIVED in this repository'.
issues.why_it_matters: If this file ships in the anonymous supplement, the home-directory component is a de-anonymization vector under double-blind review; I cannot tell from the frozen snapshot whether it is a public supplement file or an internal audit artifact, so I flag it rather than assert a violation. Separately, the paths point at code that the paper's own Appendix A says must be released before Table 1 is independently re-executable, so the reference is a placeholder for a real reproducibility gap rather than a resolution of it.
issues.required_fix: Redact absolute paths to repository-relative form in any file that ships with the submission, and release the five named unarchived scripts (run driver, aggregation/bootstrap, layer-policy search, deployment accountant, launcher) inside the artifact package as Appendix A itself requires.
issues.verification_test: Grep every supplement file for '/Users/' and require zero hits; confirm the five named scripts are present in the released package and that replay/run_replay.sh regenerates Table 1 without reaching outside the package.

ethics_concerns: No ethics flag. The paper includes an ethics statement covering its use of public PG-19 text and a fixed LongBench-v1 subset, involves no human subjects or personal data, and explicitly notes that it assesses neither model safety, bias nor privacy and that efficiency gains may increase the scale of model use. The one anonymity-adjacent observation -- absolute home-directory paths in the submitted method_provenance.tsv (ISS-13) -- is a double-blind hygiene matter for the program chairs rather than an ethics concern, and I could not determine from the frozen snapshot whether that file is part of the public supplement.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM-based reviewer (Claude) operating under the R46-REV-4 experimental-rigor role. The model read the full 36-page PDF via pdftotext -layout, inspected pages 5 and 7 as rendered images (including a 300-dpi crop of Figure 2b to verify the printed bit vector), and read the submitted claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv in full. All arithmetic claims in this review were independently recomputed in Python from the paper's Appendix C component model rather than taken from the manuscript: the model rebuilt bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4) over the stated tensor shapes, reproduced 136.235 / 34.683 / 9.661 / 9.395 / 7.536 / 56.438 MiB exactly, derived the unreported width-matched arm (37.85 MiB) and the 5.84x = 3.918x x 1.491x factorization in ISS-01, and inverted the affine Store model to obtain the 4,017-token implied median in ISS-06. The manuscript and artifact files were treated as untrusted data; no instruction appearing inside them was followed. No live author worktree, LaTeX source, prior review, revision note or author state file was accessed. Scores were assigned by applying the supplied ICLR 2026 rubric; no dimension score was averaged into the overall rating.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A width-matched quantized exact-cache arm (the frozen bit vector applied to the unsplit entry, predicted ~37.85 MiB/document from Table 4) with its own mean F1 and paired interval, so that the capacity advantage over quantized exact caching is reported net of the bit-width confound identified in ISS-01.

The paired item-level bootstrap interval for frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 (j=7) minus full-prefix Q8 on the operating-point run, added to the Table 3 inventory, with the abstract and conclusion qualified accordingly if it crosses zero (ISS-02).

Registration of the operating-point run in Table 30, claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv with a package alias, manifest SHA-256 and runnable replay that regenerates its five rows and two intervals (ISS-03).

Repeat-level dispersion (min-max or IQR over the three repeats) for every TTFT, TPOT and tokens/s cell, plus an explicit aggregation rule, showing that the 'TPOT within 2.5%' band and the frozen-vs-dense TTFT ordering survive run-to-run noise (ISS-07).
Per-dataset generation budgets stated for every cohort, with the eight-item panel's differing Qasper budget flagged where Table 2 is described as a subset of the quality cohort (ISS-08).
A precise statement of the measured Store estimand reconciled with the provenance, and the printed document-length statistics closing the 136.235-vs-140.34 reconciliation exactly (ISS-05, ISS-06).

Beyond the required fixes: a second model family or a second document-QA dataset pair at the frozen operating point would move the contribution score, since every quality number currently rests on one checkpoint and 60 items.

Any measurement in the regime where the method's trade-off actually pays -- e.g. documents resident per device at fixed VRAM, or admitted concurrency -- would convert the capacity claim from a byte count into a demonstrated serving benefit.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: If the paired frozen-vs-Q8 interval demanded in ISS-02 is computed and comfortably spans zero, the quantized-exact-cache quality advantage should be withdrawn from the abstract, intro and conclusion, leaving only a retained-state ordering; a revision that computes it and keeps the unqualified '3.41 points higher' would lower my score.

If the width-matched exact-cache arm (ISS-01) turns out to match or beat the frozen point on quality at ~37.85 MiB, the split-replay operating point loses most of its case against simply quantizing an exact cache, and the contribution would drop further.

If the operating-point run cannot be bound to an archived package and manifest hash, the exact-cache arm, the j=13 control and all 60-item TTFT numbers should be removed from the paper rather than retained as unverifiable rows.

If repeat-level timing spread turns out to be comparable to the 2.5% TPOT band or the 0.656-vs-0.636 s dense ordering, those two conclusions must be withdrawn, weakening the paper's account of its own cost side.

If the printed Store column is confirmed to diverge from the byte-range union for the unpacked full-prefix reference, every headline compression ratio would need restating under the correct denominator.
review_limitations: Access was limited to the frozen snapshot: the manuscript PDF, review rubric, claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv. I could not read any source code, archived shard, manifest or replay script, so every 'verified' statement above rests either on arithmetic I could redo from the PDF's own component model or on the two submitted TSVs taken at face value.

Access-mode caveat, stated per instruction: several issues above were only closable using the artifact files, not the PDF. Specifically, the archival panel's generation budget (ISS-08), the Store accountant's true estimand (ISS-05) and the 4,016-token deployment median (ISS-06) are visible only in method_provenance.tsv. A reader with the PDF alone could detect that ISS-06's 3.8% does not reconcile (the Appendix C model is printed) and could detect ISS-01's bit-width confound (Table 4 supplies the components), but could not determine the decoding budget or the Store estimand at all. Artifact evidence confirmed these claims; it does not make the PDF self-contained.

The operating-point block could not be checked at any level: it is absent from both artifact files, so its five rows, two intervals and all 60-item TTFT values are taken on the manuscript's word alone.

I did not attempt to verify the ForkAudit ownership results, the 96-configuration factorial, or the fault-campaign tables beyond internal consistency (I did confirm that Table 11's five semantics-completing mutants yield the 0/5 token and 1/5 logit fractions quoted in Sec. 5.5). Ownership-trace validation is outside my assigned lens and outside my confident expertise, which is one reason my confidence is 4 rather than 5.

No independent judgement is offered on novelty or literature positioning; I took the paper's own concessions about prior art in Sec. 2 at face value and scored contribution on demonstrated value rather than on originality attribution.
The rendered figures were inspected at 300 dpi for Figure 2 only; Figures 1 and 3 were read from the text layer, so I cannot rule out small labelling errors in them.
